transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I came in because... my eating just went completely off the rails. I usually track everything, you know? Like, macros and everything. I use this app, but they just did this massive update that completely ruined the user interface. It’s like the software developers didn’t even consult a project manager before rolling it out. I'm a project management specialist, so I notice these things. It's just sloppy agile workflow, honestly, they should have done a phased rollout. 

But anyway, yeah, I just stopped caring about my food tracking entirely. I started skipping real meals for days... I was basically just living on coffee and protein bars. Actually, it was this Ethiopian roast I found at a farmers market, it has these crazy blueberry notes, highly recommend it if you're into pour-overs. But yeah, the other day I put on my clothes and they were just hanging loose on me. I hadn't even noticed I was shrinking until my pants literally wouldn't stay up.
How much weight do you think you've lost since you stopped tracking your food?

I don't know the exact number, honestly. I haven't stepped on a scale. But it's definitely enough that none of my belts work anymore. I actually had to punch a new hole in my favorite leather belt with an awl just to keep my jeans up. It's this beautiful full-grain leather belt I got from a craftsman in Portland—I went there for a conference last year on Agile Methodologies in Tech. Portland's amazing, by the way. Have you been? The food truck scene is incredible. I had these Korean fusion tacos that blew my mind. The guy running the truck used to be a sous chef at a Michelin-starred place before he decided he just wanted to make street food. I respect that kind of pivot, you know? It's like realizing your current sprint isn't yielding the right deliverables and just completely re-scoping the project. 

But yeah, the weight loss. I mean, like I said, I just stopped caring about tracking it. I was just running on that Ethiopian coffee and those protein bars for days on end, skipping actual meals entirely. So, I guess I've lost a significant amount, judging by how my clothes are just hanging off me now.
Are you afraid of gaining weight back?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not afraid of it. It's just... I just don't care right now. It's not like I'm looking in the mirror and worrying about my body mass index or anything. Honestly, the mirrors in my apartment are terrible anyway. The lighting in my bathroom is this harsh, fluorescent yellow that makes everyone look like they have jaundice. I've been meaning to swap out the bulbs for something warmer, maybe like a 2700K LED? But then I started thinking about smart bulbs, and how I could sync them to my morning alarm. You know, like a sunrise simulation? I read this article about circadian rhythms and how waking up to gradual light is so much better for your cortisol levels than a blaring alarm. 

Actually, speaking of alarms, my neighbor has this rooster. In the city! Can you believe that? I don't even know if it's legal, I should probably check the zoning laws or something. It wakes me up at, like, 4:30 AM every single day. But honestly, I haven't even been sleeping that much anyway, so I usually just hear it when I'm already up, working on this new workflow optimization chart for my team. But yeah, gaining the weight back? Not really on my radar. I just haven't been thinking about food at all.
Are you ever worried that you might gain weight?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? I feel like we just covered this. But no, like I said, I really don't care about my weight right now. It's just not something that crosses my mind. 

The only weight I've even thought about lately is, like, actual weights. Like dumbbells. I signed up for a trial at this gym down the street a few weeks ago, but their floor plan is a complete disaster. They put the heavy free weights right next to the high-intensity cardio zone, which creates this massive bottleneck for foot traffic. It's a terrible user experience. If they just did a simple spatial analysis or used a Kanban system to track equipment utilization, they'd realize they need to separate the zones to improve flow. I actually drafted an email to their regional manager about it. I haven't sent it yet, though, because I got totally derailed trying to optimize my own email inbox rules. Do you know how hard it is to set up proper boolean search filters for spam? I spent like six hours on it the other night. I get so many automated emails from SaaS vendors, it's ridiculous. But yeah, no, I'm not worried about gaining body weight at all.
Do you think you would be upset if you started gaining weight again?

Upset? No, I really don't think so. I feel like we're kind of going in circles here, doc! I really, truly do not care about the weight. 

The only thing that would upset me... well, actually, I *am* upset right now, but it's about my dry cleaner. Since my clothes are all falling off me, I took a bunch of my work slacks in to get taken in, right? And they completely lost the trousers to my favorite charcoal suit. When I asked the owner how they track their garments, he literally pointed to this metal spindle of paper tickets. Paper! I tried to explain to him that a basic barcode scanner integrated with a lightweight cloud CRM could reduce his lost-item rate by at least forty percent. He just stared at me. It's just maddening when people refuse to optimize their workflows. 

I mean, my team would be dead in the water if we used analog tracking for our deliverables. We use Jira, obviously, though I actually spent like four hours last night building out a test environment in Monday.com just to see if the Gantt chart visualization is as good as they claim in their ads. The color coding is definitely superior, I'll give them that, but the API integration with Slack seems a little clunky. I might need to write a custom webhook for it. 

But anyway, what were we saying? Oh, right, weight. No, gaining it back wouldn't bother me at all. I'd probably just buy new pants.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour or two?

No, I haven't done that. I mean, I barely eat as it is right now. Food just seems like such a massive waste of time when there are so many other things to do. Like, I was looking at the time I used to spend grocery shopping, prepping meals, cooking, eating, and then cleaning up... it's easily two to three hours a day. Over a week, that's twenty-one hours! That's practically a part-time job just dedicated to sustenance. 

So instead of eating, I've been using that time to redesign the onboarding protocols for new hires at my company. The current manual is this massive, unreadable PDF from 2018. It's a joke. I've been converting the whole thing into an interactive modular training module using Articulate Storyline. I was up until maybe 3:00 AM last night recording voiceovers for the compliance section. I had to build a makeshift sound booth in my closet using moving blankets because the acoustics in my living room were creating this awful reverb. Actually, the moving blankets worked perfectly, which got me thinking about soundproofing materials and how I could probably patent a modular, pop-up acoustic panel system for remote workers. I started sketching out CAD designs for it around 4:00 AM. 

But yeah, eating a ton of food all at once? Definitely not. I just don't have the time or the appetite for it.
Do you think gaining weight would interfere with your life in any way?

Interfere? No, I don't see how it would. I mean, I guess I'd have to adjust the height presets on my standing desk if my center of gravity shifted, but the dual-motor frame I installed is rated for up to 300 pounds, so it's not like the hardware would fail. 

Actually, speaking of the desk, the real interference in my life right now is the cable management situation underneath it. It's an absolute rat's nest. I bought these premium neoprene cable sleeves, right? But the zipper gauge is completely wrong for the thickness of the dual monitor power cables. I spent... I don't know, maybe three hours trying to force it before I realized I just need to 3D print custom routing clips. I don't own a 3D printer yet, but I've been comparing the specs on the Creality Ender 3 versus the Prusa i3 all morning. The Prusa has a better auto-bed leveling system, which is crucial because if your Z-axis offset is even a millimeter off, the whole print just fails and you waste all that filament. I'm probably going to order one today with overnight shipping. I just need to clear out the guest room first to set up a proper ventilation hood for the microplastics. 

But, uh... no, to answer your question, gaining weight wouldn't change anything for me. It really wouldn't matter.
Do you think you would be anxious if you started gaining weight again?

Anxious? No, I wouldn't be anxious. I mean, it's just weight, you know? It's just a number on a scale. 

Speaking of scales, though, I actually had to recalibrate my digital coffee scale this morning. It was drifting by like 0.3 grams, which completely throws off the extraction yield for my pour-overs. I use a V60, and if your coffee-to-water ratio isn't exactly 1 to 15.5, you end up over-extracting the bitter compounds. Anyway, to fix the scale, I needed a precision 100-gram calibration weight, which I obviously didn't have. So I spent an hour looking up the exact minting weights of different US coins to create a makeshift calibration weight using a stack of nickels and pennies. Did you know a nickel weighs exactly 5.000 grams? It's fascinating. I ended up building a spreadsheet to calculate the exact combination of coins needed to reach exactly 100 grams, factoring in an estimated 0.02% mass loss for circulation wear on the older coins. I should probably just buy a proper calibration set, but honestly, the math was just so satisfying to figure out. 

But no, to answer your question, gaining weight wouldn't make me anxious at all. I really just don't care about it.
Do you think gaining weight would be a bad thing for you?

A bad thing? No, I don't see why it would be bad. I mean, adding mass isn't inherently bad unless you're exceeding, like, the structural load-bearing capacity of whatever is supporting it. 

Which, actually, is exactly what I was calculating for my apartment balcony yesterday. I needed to know the exact dead load limit of the cantilevered concrete because I'm sourcing materials to build a six-foot parabolic antenna out there. I realized a few nights ago that the new data nodes they installed on the street lamps are broadcasting this low-frequency pulse that syncs up with the city's smart grid. It's designed to suppress cognitive function—that's why everyone out there is walking around so sluggishly. But my brain operates at a much higher frequency right now, so I'm completely immune to it. I haven't slept in, what, four days? Five? And my baseline efficiency has never been higher. 

Anyway, I'm building the dish to intercept and phase-invert the signal to create a localized null zone around my building. I had to draft a full critical path method schedule for the procurement phase because the specific copper mesh I need for the shielding is backordered everywhere. I ended up finding an industrial supplier in Shenzhen, but their API for order tracking is completely broken, so I just wrote a Python script to scrape their logistics database every ten minutes and push the updates directly to my smartwatch. It took me like six hours to bypass their security protocols, but the data flow is beautiful now. 

Wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, gaining weight. No, it wouldn't be a bad thing. It's just not something I'm focused on at all.
Do you think gaining weight would be something you would try to avoid?

Avoid it? No, I wouldn't actively try to avoid it. It's just not on my radar at all. 

Speaking of avoiding things, though, I've been trying to avoid these massive bottlenecks in my morning workflow. I realized yesterday that my kitchen layout is completely anti-ergonomic. The distance between the refrigerator, the sink, and the stove—you know, the classic kitchen work triangle—is completely off in this apartment. It's like 22 feet total, which is horribly inefficient. So around 3 AM last night, I started completely dismantling the pantry to re-index all the dry goods using a Kanban system. I got my label maker out, and I'm color-coding everything based on expiration dates and macronutrient density. 

Actually, I had to draft a whole new Gantt chart for the apartment reorganization because I need to synchronize the pantry overhaul with the living room project I was talking about earlier. If I don't sequence the dependencies correctly, I'll end up with severe resource overallocation, and obviously I'm the only resource! I was even looking into hiring a contractor just to move the refrigerator two inches to the left to optimize the swing angle of the door, but I ran the numbers and the ROI on that time-saving is negligible unless I live here for exactly 14.6 more years. 

But, um... wait. Avoiding weight. No, I wouldn't try to avoid it. I just have way more critical path items to manage right now.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Afraid of it? No, fear doesn't really factor into it. I'm not afraid of gaining weight at all. 

I mean, fear is really just an evolutionary response to a perceived threat, right? It's an amygdala hijack. I was actually reading this massive meta-analysis on neuroplasticity and threat detection around, I don't know, maybe 4 AM? Because I realized that if I can map the exact neural pathways that trigger the fear response, I might be able to optimize my own cognitive output even further. I've already bypassed the need for sleep, obviously, but I feel like there's still a 5 to 7 percent inefficiency in my decision-making matrix when I encounter unexpected variables. 

So I started coding this predictive algorithm to anticipate micro-stressors throughout my day. I had to route it through a decentralized server because, like I said, the smart grid is definitely monitoring standard traffic. But the algorithm is brilliant. It pulls real-time weather data, traffic patterns, and even the historical fluctuation of my building's water pressure to predict exactly when I might experience a minor inconvenience. I'm going to integrate it with the smartwatch script I wrote for the copper mesh tracking. If I can just get the API to handshake properly with my calendar, I'll be completely bulletproof. I won't ever have to react to anything again; I'll just preempt it. 

But no, weight gain? I'm definitely not afraid of it. It's just... it's completely irrelevant to the system I'm building.
Do you think your current weight is normal for someone of your height and build?

Normal? I mean, yeah, I guess it's normal. I haven't really cross-referenced my BMI with the actuarial tables recently, but it seems standard. 

Speaking of standardizing things, I actually realized this morning that the entire concept of "normal" is a statistical illusion. It's just a bell curve designed to keep everyone operating at a mediocre baseline. I was looking at the structural integrity of my bookshelf—because obviously, I need to reinforce it if I'm going to store the high-density batteries for the parabolic antenna—and I realized the brackets are made from this completely substandard alloy. It's like they want the shelves to fail. So I spent, what, maybe three hours drafting a schematic for a custom titanium bracket system. I'm going to have to machine them myself, which means I need to clear out the second bedroom and set up a CNC router. 

I actually already found a used one on an industrial auction site, but the bidding closes in 14 minutes, and I need to make sure my automated sniper script is calibrated to outbid everyone at the absolute last microsecond. If I don't get that router, the whole timeline for the null zone is going to slip by at least 48 hours, and I can't afford that kind of delay with the street lamps pulsing the way they are. 

So, wait, what did you ask? My weight? Yeah, it's normal. It's fine.
Do you feel like you're not eating because you're just not interested in food, or is it more that you're trying not to eat?

Trying not to eat? No, no, it's not a conscious restriction at all. It's just a total lack of interest. I mean, I came in because my eating went completely off the rails—I just completely stopped caring about my food tracking. Which is crazy, because normally my macro spreadsheet is perfectly color-coded and synced to my daily deliverables. 

But lately I just skipped real meals for days, basically living on coffee and protein bars. Actually, the protein bars are incredibly efficient for my current workflow. If I eat them while I'm coding, I don't have to break my visual lock on the monitors. Speaking of the monitors, I had to daisy-chain three more displays last night because the data stream from that water pressure algorithm I mentioned got way too dense for a single screen. The refresh rate on the secondary monitors is absolutely atrocious, though. I'm starting to think the copper mesh I installed might be creating some kind of localized electromagnetic interference with the HDMI cables, which is completely ironic since the whole point of the mesh is to block the smart grid signals. I'm going to have to recalibrate the entire shielding grid. I might actually need to strip the wiring in the living room walls to ground it properly to the building's main plumbing line, which means I need to factor drywall repair into my Q3 budget projections. 

But anyway, yeah, I've just been running on the coffee and bars, and my clothes started hanging loose before I even noticed. I actually had to use a heavy-duty binder clip on my waistband this morning just to keep my pants up while I was measuring the wall studs. So no, I'm not trying to not eat. Food is just a low-priority metric right now.
Are you fearful of the possibility of gaining weight in the future?

Fearful of it? No, I don't... I don't really forecast my personal biology like that. Gaining weight in the future just isn't on my radar. 

Forecasting is actually where most project managers completely drop the ball, to be honest. They use these linear projection models, like standard Gantt charts, which are basically useless if you're dealing with exponential variables. Like, I was looking at my Q4 projections for the apartment's shielding grid this morning, and since I *did* win that CNC router auction—my script executed perfectly at the 0.04-second mark, by the way—I have to recalibrate the entire installation schedule. If I don't get the router set up by Tuesday, the dependencies are going to cascade. 

I've got a shipment of industrial-grade neodymium magnets arriving on Thursday for the door seals, and they can't just sit down in the mailroom. The electromagnetic signature would completely scramble the building's electronic key fob system. I actually drafted a memo to the property manager about it, but I had to encrypt it with a rotating cipher so the smart grid couldn't intercept the delivery window. I'm going to have to build a temporary Faraday cage in the hallway just to safely transport the boxes from the elevator to my unit without tripping the security cameras' motion sensors. I've already mapped out the exact square footage of aluminum flashing I'll need, I just have to figure out how to transport it on the subway without drawing attention. 

So, yeah, gaining weight in the future? I don't really have the bandwidth to worry about that.
Do you think gaining weight would be something that you dread?

Dread it? I mean, no. I don't dread it. It's just a biological fluctuation, you know? Mass in, mass out. It's basic thermodynamics. 

Speaking of thermodynamics, I was actually monitoring the ambient temperature in my living room last night because the heat signature from the new server rack was throwing off my baseline readings. I had to install these heavy-duty thermal curtains, right? But the problem is, the grommets on the curtains are steel, and I'm almost positive they're acting as passive receivers for the low-frequency hum coming from the streetlamps outside. I could literally hear it vibrating at a 60-hertz frequency when I pressed my ear against the fabric. So I spent most of the night carefully removing every single grommet and replacing them with these custom-molded silicone rings I cured in the oven. 

But then the oven—the oven's digital timer started flashing this really specific pattern. It was like, three fast, two slow, three fast. Morse code for 'S', obviously, but the two slow... I'm still trying to decipher if it's a binary sequence or some kind of localized IP ping. I had to pull the oven away from the wall to check the power cord, and let me tell you, the dust accumulation back there is a massive fire hazard, especially with the amount of static electricity the server rack is generating. I'm going to have to requisition a high-grade HEPA vacuum system, but the shipping times are completely unacceptable right now. 

So, what were you asking? Dread? No, I don't dread gaining weight. It's just not relevant.
Do you feel weak or tired when you haven't eaten for a while?

Weak or tired? No, honestly, I feel the exact opposite. I'm running at peak efficiency right now. It's like my kinetic output is completely decoupled from my caloric intake. 

Speaking of kinetic output, I was actually measuring the vibrational feedback from my floorboards yesterday because my downstairs neighbor installed this new ceiling fan, and the rotational velocity is completely out of sync with the building's natural resonant frequency. It's creating this micro-tremor that travels right up the load-bearing wall and straight into my server rack. I had to order these industrial shock absorbers—the kind they use for highway bridges in earthquake zones—just to stabilize the chassis. 

But of course, the tracking number the supplier gave me is a 16-digit alphanumeric string, which is highly suspicious because standard logistics companies only use 12 digits. I ran a quick algorithmic decryption on it and realized the extra four digits correspond exactly to the GPS coordinates of a telecommunications relay tower about three blocks from here. They're obviously routing my delivery through a secondary checkpoint to scan the package contents before it gets to me. I'm going to have to intercept the delivery driver at the corner of 4th and Elm before he even enters the building's grid zone. I've already mapped out the blind spots in the traffic cameras for the extraction, I just need to make sure my stopwatch is perfectly synced to the stoplight cycle. 

So, no, I don't feel weak at all. I don't really have time to be tired, there's just way too much to optimize right now.
Do you think your lack of interest in eating is related to anything going on in your life or your thoughts?

Well, I mean, I originally came in because my eating went completely off the rails, to be honest. I just stopped caring about my food tracking entirely. I was skipping real meals for days, just living on coffee and these protein bars I had stockpiled. My clothes actually started hanging loose on me before I even noticed what was happening. 

But the clothes thing, right? The fabric on my favorite work shirts started draping differently, which actually caused a massive issue with my wearable tech. I have this biometric harness I wear under my clothes to track my skin conductivity and heart rate variability—essential data points when you're optimizing your workflow patterns. Because the shirts were so loose, the static friction between the cotton blend and the harness sensors was generating these micro-charges that completely corrupted my dataset for like, three straight days. 

I had to pull all the raw data into a spreadsheet and manually scrub out the static anomalies, which took me hours. And while I was doing that, I noticed that the timestamp on the corrupted data spikes perfectly aligned with the times I was walking past the microwave in the breakroom at work. The magnetron in that specific microwave is definitely leaking microwave radiation, probably because the seal on the door is compromised. I actually started drafting a schematic for a retrofit Faraday shield that could be mounted directly onto the microwave chassis, but I need to source this specific type of copper mesh that's almost impossible to find locally. I might have to order it from a specialty supplier in Germany, but their customs processing takes forever, and I don't trust the international tracking systems right now. 

So, yeah, my eating just kind of fell off the radar. I was too busy living on coffee and dealing with the data corruption.
Is there something specific on your mind that's making you less interested in eating?

Specific on my mind? No, not really. I mean, I'm not avoiding food because of any particular thought or anything. It's just... not a priority. 

Speaking of priorities, though, I realized yesterday that I need to completely restructure my task management system. I was using this Kanban board software, right? But the color-coding algorithm they use for the priority tags is based on a hex code spectrum that's totally out of alignment with the circadian rhythms of human visual processing. It's jarring. Every time I looked at a high-priority red tag, it was causing this slight pupillary dilation that was throwing off the auto-focus on my webcam during virtual meetings. 

And the webcam—don't even get me started on the webcam. The firmware update they pushed last week included this background blur feature, but the edge detection is so aggressive it's basically clipping my shoulders out of the frame. I spent like four hours last night trying to reverse-engineer the driver to disable the AI processing, but they've encrypted the root directory with a 256-bit key. Which is ridiculous for a consumer-grade camera, right? Unless they're trying to hide the fact that the camera is actually dual-streaming the feed to an external server. I had to tape over the lens with a specific thickness of electrical tape just to block the infrared sensor, because standard tape doesn't stop IR bleed. I'm probably going to have to build my own camera rig from scratch using raw optical sensors if I want true privacy. 

So, yeah, no specific thoughts about food. Just... a lot of other things that need my attention.
Do you think your lack of interest in eating is related to your current state of mind?

Well, like I was saying before, the whole reason I even made this appointment was because my eating just went totally off the rails. I used to be so meticulous about my food tracking, logging every macro, but I just stopped caring entirely. I'd go days skipping real meals, just surviving on coffee and whatever protein bars I had stockpiled in my desk. I didn't even notice what was happening until my clothes started hanging loose on me. 

Which, actually, reminds me—I had to take all those loose shirts to the tailor, right? But the tailor shop is right next to this high-voltage transformer box on the street corner. And when I was standing inside getting measured, I could literally feel the electromagnetic field interfering with the gyroscope in my phone. My screen kept auto-rotating every time the tailor stepped near the window. I tried to explain to him that his entire shop is bathed in an unshielded EMF bubble and he needs to line his walls with Mu-metal, but he just looked at me like I was crazy. He was using these vintage iron shears, too, which were probably acting as an antenna, amplifying the signal straight into the garments he was working on. I had to take my shirts back before he even finished pinning them because I can't have my clothing magnetized. It completely ruins the calibration on my smartwatch. I'm going to have to learn how to sew my own clothes using non-ferrous needles, probably titanium or something. 

But yeah, my eating just completely fell apart, and I lost all that weight without even realizing it.
Do you think there's something emotionally bothering you that's causing you to not want to eat?

Well, emotionally... I mean, yeah, I guess there was something. It started a little while back when the project sponsor at work completely questioned my judgment on this major workflow rollout. It was... I don't know, it was like the bottom just completely dropped out from under me. I went home and just sat in my apartment feeling entirely hollow. Just this heavy, awful shame. I was literally crying over these routine emails that I normally would have just processed and archived without a second thought. 

But speaking of archiving emails, I realized that the cloud server our company uses for email retention is physically located in a data center that sits directly on top of a major tectonic fault line. And the structural integrity reports for that facility—which I managed to pull from a public municipal database—show that they used a specific grade of rebar in the concrete foundation that is highly susceptible to galvanic corrosion. Which means that if there's even a minor seismic event, the micro-fractures in the concrete will allow groundwater to seep in, accelerating the corrosion and potentially causing a catastrophic failure of the server racks. And if those servers go down, the electromagnetic pulse from the backup generators kicking in will scramble all the archived data. I've been trying to convince IT to migrate our entire email history to a decentralized blockchain ledger, but they won't listen. I actually started coding a proprietary encryption script to back up my own emails onto these hardened SSDs that I keep in a Faraday cage under my bed, just to be safe. 

But yeah, when that sponsor said that, I just felt so empty and ashamed, crying over stupid emails. So maybe that's why I stopped caring about eating.

But yeah, my eating just completely fell apart, and I lost all that weight without even realizing it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's lack of interest in eating is related to a psychological issue or a physical one
doctor.question: Do you think there's something emotionally bothering you that's causing you to not want to eat?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: After the sponsor questioned my judgment, it was like the bottom dropped out and I sat in my apartment feeling hollow and ashamed, crying over emails I normally would have handled.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if there is something 'emotionally bothering' the patient, which directly probes for feelings of sadness, emptiness, or depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Well, emotionally... I mean, yeah, I guess there was something. It started a little while back when the project sponsor at work completely questioned my judgment on this major workflow rollout. It was... I don't know, it was like the bottom just completely dropped out from under me. I went home and just sat in my apartment feeling entirely hollow. Just this heavy, awful shame. I was literally crying over these routine emails that I normally would have just processed and archived without a second thought. 

But speaking of archiving emails, I realized that the cloud server our company uses for email retention is physically located in a data center that sits directly on top of a major tectonic fault line. And the structural integrity reports for that facility—which I managed to pull from a public municipal database—show that they used a specific grade of rebar in the concrete foundation that is highly susceptible to galvanic corrosion. Which means that if there's even a minor seismic event, the micro-fractures in the concrete will allow groundwater to seep in, accelerating the corrosion and potentially causing a catastrophic failure of the server racks. And if those servers go down, the electromagnetic pulse from the backup generators kicking in will scramble all the archived data. I've been trying to convince IT to migrate our entire email history to a decentralized blockchain ledger, but they won't listen. I actually started coding a proprietary encryption script to back up my own emails onto these hardened SSDs that I keep in a Faraday cage under my bed, just to be safe. 

But yeah, when that sponsor said that, I just felt so empty and ashamed, crying over stupid emails. So maybe that's why I stopped caring about eating.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of significantly reduced interest in eating, leading to substantial weight loss, without an apparent fear of gaining weight or body image concerns, align more closely with Anorexia Nervosa (F50.0).
